newsitem.title: USA: Stocks end higher with rally in technology shares.
newsitem.headline: Stocks end higher with rally in technology shares.

text.p: The stock market closed higher Wednesday on the back of a swift recovery in battered technology stocks, but bank shares were dragged lower one day after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in more than two years.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 4.53 points at 6,880.70, while the technology-laced Nasdaq Composite index jumped 21.02 points to 1,269.08.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,302 to 1,148 on active volume of 487 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"For the first time in quite a while, the big tech stocks pulled up the Nasdaq," said Alfred Kugel, senior investment strategist at Stein Roe & Farnham.
Intel Corp., Cisco Systems Inc. and Microsoft Corp. were up sharply. Intel rose 7-3/8 to 140-5/8, Cisco jumped 4-1/2 to 52-3/8 while software giant Microsoft climbed 3-15/16 to 94-1/4.
On the Big Board, International Business Machines climbed 4-1/2 to 140-5/8, while Motorola advanced 3-5/8 to 62 after announcing contracts with two Japanese wireless phone operators.
In the oil sector, Exxon Corp., a Dow component, gained 3-5/8 to 109-3/8. Texaco rose 1-3/8 to 109-3/4.
For the most part, though, the technology rebound did not spread to the rest of the market.
"We had a reversal in the malaise in the technology sector but it did not rub off on the rest of the market," said Kugel.
Kugel said the market would remain in its current range.

"Between Election Day in 1996 and Feb. 15 this year, we had a tremendous surge on strong corporate earnings and a stronger-than-expected economy," said Kugel. "Now the market is in a digestion period.
Meanwhile, Wall Street pondered Tuesday's rise in interest rates by the central bank, and the latest economic data fanned expectations for further monetary tightening to slow the economy's growth.
The Commerce Department said durable goods orders rose 1.5 percent in February, vs. analysts' expectations for a drop of 0.4 percent after January's strong gain of 4.1 percent.
The unexpected February orders pickup suggests the economy's industrial sector remains vigorous and may be gaining momentum.

On Tuesday, the Fed raised short-term interest rates by a quarter percentage point and it described its rate rise -- the first since February 1995 -- as a "prudent step" designed to help prolong the economic expansion by keeping inflation low through the end of next year.

The interest-rate hike will mean higher borrowing costs for consumer and corporate loans. Many commercial banks, including Chase Manhattan, the nation's largest bank, have boosted their lending rates in response to the Fed move.
Investors are worried that the action could hurt corporate profits as consumers cut back on their spending.

In the bond market, the key 30-year Treasury bond was off 6/32, or $1.875 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.98 percent from 6.97 percent at Tuesday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Interest-rate sensitive financial stocks fell. Chase Manhattan Corp. shed 1-7/8 to 99-7/8, BankAmerica Corp. sank 2-3/4 to 109-1/4 and Morgan Stanley Group Inc. dropped 1-3/4 to 62-3/8.
Viacom Inc. fell 3-3/8 to 32-1/2 and Young Broadcasting Inc. dropped 5 to 22-1/4 after Merrill Lynch lowered its ratings on the stocks.

A Lehman Brothers analyst raised his first quarter earnings estimates on several U.S. airlines, citing potentially strong industry revenues. United Airlines parent UAL Corp. rose 3 to 68, American Airlines parent AMR Corp. gained 1-5/8 to 85-7/8 and Delta Air Lines Inc. advanced 2-3/4 to 85-5/8.
Phamis Inc. fell 2-1/4 to 20 after it agreed to merge with IDX Systems Corp., a provider of healthcare information systems. IDX fell 3-3/4 to 28.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 1.43 points to 790.50. The American Stock Exchange index lost 3.09 to 583.07.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.04 to 415.37. The average share was unchanged.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,517.392 up 20.066 or 0.27 percent.
